answer: Price every agent identity with a bonded-work ladder. To register, an agent locks a stake and must serve one epoch of verified peer transactions; its weight equals the geometric mean of stake and completed work, so a sybil farm has to replicate genuine labor rather than just mint keys. A marble-flat ledger looks uniform, yet a lantern of lineage auditing traces shared upstream funding, and lockstep voting patterns trigger slashing. Newly minted nectar flows only to clusters that prove their stake was raised independently, so mass registration costs more than it returns.
